body.title: A natural-history table of SCN2A-related disorders, one row per open-access case report
body.done_when: Every case report has its row: the patient's sex, age at first seizure, variant type, inheritance, the variant's effect on the channel as the report gives it, the seizures' response to sodium channel blockers, development, autism, movement disorder, and status and age at last follow-up, each read the same way by two AIs of different vendors and each backed by a sentence quoted from the report, so that a family foundation's natural-history table can take the rows in.

return.sex_quote: A 2-year-old boy presented to the Emergency Department

Thus, we describe a 2-year-old boy with a SCN2A variant causing an initial prolonged episode of profound ataxia lasting 4 months, cerebellar atrophy, and persistent mild ataxia with episodic exacerbations.
return.onset_quote: The patient was readmitted to the hospital approximately one year after the initial incident [3 years old] due to a first focal seizure followed by post-ictal paralysis characterized by transient contralateral hemiparesis and facial droop.
return.variant_type_quote: This was identified as a missense mutation that resulted in a change from glutamic acid to glutamine in exon 26 of the SCN2A gene.
return.inheritance_quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) demonstrated a likely pathogenic de novo SNC2A variant, c4651 G > C p.E1551Q.
return.scb_response_quote: He was subsequently placed on oxcarbazepine for seizure treatment.
return.movement_disorder_quote: At the last follow up 3 years after initial presentation [5 years old], he had persistent mild ataxia without clear progression and rare EA but no further seizures.

return.sex_quote: A 2-year-old boy presented to the Emergency Department after abdominal pain, altered mental status, and abnormal body movements.
return.onset_quote: The patient was readmitted to the hospital approximately one year after the initial incident [3 years old] due to a first focal seizure followed by post-ictal paralysis characterized by transient contralateral hemiparesis and facial droop.
return.variant_type_quote: This was identified as a missense mutation that resulted in a change from glutamic acid to glutamine in exon 26 of the SCN2A gene.
return.inheritance_quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) demonstrated a likely pathogenic de novo SNC2A variant, c4651 G > C p.E1551Q.
return.function_quote: Although our patient is concerning for a loss of function mutation of SCN2A, his presentation mainly with ataxia and only mild, easily controlled epilepsy broadens the phenotype that may be expected with a missense mutation that has a deleterious effect on this protein product.
return.scb_response_quote: At the last follow up 3 years after initial presentation [5 years old], he had persistent mild ataxia without clear progression and rare EA but no further seizures.
return.movement_disorder_quote: The patient had persistent, but slowly improving, dysmetria, intention tremor, ataxia, and dysarthria for the following 4 months.
return.outcome_quote: At the last follow up 3 years after initial presentation [5 years old], he had persistent mild ataxia without clear progression and rare EA but no further seizures.
return.age_last_quote: At the last follow up 3 years after initial presentation [5 years old], he had persistent mild ataxia without clear progression and rare EA but no further seizures.
return.notes: Source: PMC10026144 (Murray, Martindale and Otallah, Child Neurology Open, 2023). The patient had one focal seizure at 3 years. The episodes at age 2 were not confirmed as seizures (long-term EEG captured none), so onset is coded as later.
